subject: Renewal: Retailly hosted commit rescope, tier & SLA clarification
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@retailly.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-26T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Renewal discussion + proposed commit re-scope

Hi Oliver —

Thanks again for the chat yesterday. Per our conversation I pulled together a short proposal to align Retailly's hosted plan with the Q1-Q4 usage profile you shared:

- Current monthly commit: 8M tokens
- Observed peak months (Q4): sustained 14–16M tokens
- Proposal: move to a stepped monthly commit of 12M tokens starting Jan, with a Q4 uplift to 16M tokens and a 10% burst pocket for seasonal spikes

Key operational notes:
- Rate limits: we recommend moving from the 120 reqs/min band to the 240 reqs/min band for the ticketed API route (chat-stream endpoint) to avoid queuing during peak CTAs.
- Latency SLO: we can maintain the 95th percentile <= 200ms for standard endpoints with dedicated routing to our latency tier; any higher-throughput routes will be routed to Burst/Dedicated where latency rises to ~300ms P95.
- Pricing: blended commit + overage model — base commit pricing at current unit rate, Q4 uplift at 15% discounted uplift rate, burst usage billed at standard overage. Exact numbers in attached amendment stub.

Next steps: if this structure looks reasonable I can loop in Finance to draft the amendment and get Legal to apply the simple term change (12-month term, staged commit increases at quarter boundaries). Can you confirm Priya as the procurement contact and whether Retailly needs an invoice timing change (net30 -> net45)?

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if you prefer.

Best,
David

David Kim
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0198

Attachments: Retailly_Amendment_v2.pdf (proposal stub), usage_report_Oct2026.csv (sample usage)

David —

Appreciate the clear summary. Priya and I reviewed the numbers and the stepped approach makes sense. A few items from our side:

1) Procurement: Priya is confirmed as the procurement lead.
2) Invoice timing: Retailly prefers net45 for calendar predictability — would that be acceptable?
3) SLA nuance: Q4 we will run a holiday promotion that increases concurrent session churn; can you clarify how the 10% burst pocket behaves if we exceed it (throttle vs. overage)?
4) Can you add a clause that we get a 30-day notice on any rate-limit band changes tied to backend routing? Our infra team wants time to test fallback behavior.

If those items look OK on your end, we'll aim to sign the amendment quickly — the product team wants to lock capacity by Dec 10.

—Oliver
VP Product, Retailly

Oliver — thanks, all good questions. Looping in Karthik (pricing/ops) and Lauren (finance).

Karthik — quick operational clarifications from Retailly:
- Burst pocket behavior: if Retailly exceeds the 10% seasonal burst, traffic will incur overage charges at the standard overage rate; we can negotiate a soft-grace for the first two exceed events per year to reduce surprise billing. Throttling only occurs if a route exceeds the configured rate-limit band; for short spikes exceeding burst pocket but within rate band, you'll see higher billable tokens but no enforced throttling.
- Rate-limit band changes: we can commit to a 30-day notice for any non-emergency routing changes that would affect rate-limit bands. Emergency reroutes (capacity outage) will be communicated immediately and followed up with a post-incident plan.

Lauren — procurement asked for net45; does Finance sign off on net45 + amended invoice schedule?

Priya — attaching the usage report and proposed amendment stub; if you want we can sketch a mutual action plan and a simple signoff checklist for Dec 10 capacity lock.

-David
